UnitStatement: The DEL-12-04 control defines bounded reference-handling behavior for private libraries, private path references, secret-like fields, and credential placeholders.
The reference-handling control is local-first, metadata-only, and uses invented fixtures only.
The control does not store usable credential material, private-library payloads, private project payloads, protected standards content, or proprietary source content.
Reference records carry explicit metadata including reference ID, record kind, label, and storage locality.
Reference record metadata includes privacy classification, redistribution status, and review disposition.
Reference record metadata includes source/provenance state and a source note.
Reference record metadata includes checksum and checksum status where available.
Reference record metadata includes a value descriptor for an opaque placeholder or symbolic path class.
Reference records include unresolved TBD entries that must remain visible to reviewers.
The implementation does not infer permission from filename patterns or engineering-looking values.
Absent, unknown, or TBD metadata remains an explicit warning or blocking finding depending on release context.
Public reports may retain metadata-only private-library references (invented name, version, checksum, source note) while emitting warnings.
Public fixtures are stricter and block private references; fixture records should use invented public-example metadata instead of private-kind references.
All release contexts block secret-like material embedded in a reference record.
All release contexts block private-library payload data embedded in a reference record.
All release contexts block private path payload data embedded in a reference record.
All release contexts block generic payload markers, including contains_payload and payload_present.
All release contexts block cloud or network references.
All release contexts block external secret-manager assumptions.
All release contexts block direct SQL, raw SQLite, table-handle, or connection-string markers.
All release contexts block storage-bypass markers that would skip application-service, provenance, redaction, or local-first storage controls.
All release contexts block rejected, quarantined, or suspected protected source disposition.
Concrete path indicators are reduced to safe metadata and must not emit direct paths in guard manifests or diagnostics.
Public, shared-model, and downstream-tool contexts additionally block private data whose redistribution status remains unknown or TBD.
Public and shared release contexts also block private data with unresolved redistribution status or unresolved privacy classification.
Local/private use of private metadata requires explicit local/private intent and still emits a warning.
The control does not select operating-system storage roots.
The control does not integrate an external secret manager.
The control does not authorize direct SQL, raw SQLite access, hosted databases, cloud sync, or storage bypasses.
The control does not finalize encryption or key-management policy.
The control does not move quarantine material.
The control does not transmit data to a cloud service.
The control does not decide legal rights.
The control does not assert professional approval or code-compliance status.

Diagnostics identify reference IDs and reason codes only, and must not print secret-like values, private path payloads, private library payloads, private project payloads, or protected source content.
DEL-12-04 implementation changes should be checked for traceability to DEL-12-04, PKG-12, SOW-040, SOW-029, and OBJ-010.
DEL-12-04 changes should be checked for deterministic classification for repeated invented inputs.
DEL-12-04 changes should be checked for metadata-only manifests that preserve checksum, source note, classification, warning severity, and unresolved TBD markers.

DEL-12-04 changes should produce blocking diagnostics for public fixture/export attempts containing secret-like values, private path payloads, private-library payloads, or unknown-redistribution private data.
DEL-12-04 changes should produce blocking diagnostics for payload markers, cloud/network markers, external secret-manager markers, direct SQL/raw SQLite markers, and storage-bypass markers.
DEL-12-04 changes should be checked for safe metadata reduction for concrete path indicators.

DEL-12-04 changes should be checked for absence of usable credential material, private payloads, protected standards content, cloud behavior, external secret-manager behavior, or professional authority assertions.
